patterns.usage_note: Listing と joins nouns and claims the list is exhaustive: パンと卵 means those two and nothing else, whereas や names only samples and leaves the rest open. It repeats between every item (AとBとC); modern usage normally drops the と after the last item, though the fuller AとBと(を) survives in formal and older writing. The comitative と also follows a noun, so tell them apart by structure — listing と yields a single NP that fills one slot (パンと卵を買う), while comitative と names a companion to the verb (友達と行く). The quotative と attaches to a clause.

examples.ruby: 朝[あさ]はパンと卵[たまご]と牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]で済[す]ませる。
examples.english: For breakfast I make do with bread, eggs, and milk.

examples.ruby: 荷物[にもつ]は財布[さいふ]と鍵[かぎ]と携帯[けいたい]を持[も]って出[で]た。
examples.english: For luggage I took my wallet, keys, and phone and headed out.

examples.ruby: 週末[しゅうまつ]は大阪[おおさか]と京都[きょうと]を回[まわ]る予定[よてい]だ。
examples.english: Over the weekend I plan to make the rounds of Osaka and Kyoto.
